- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 2–4 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5/1.0/0.0), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment polarity.
